contexts.description: The cross-cutting layer that fires and tracks async AI jobs, routes script and frame-direction generation to server APIs, and installs the test harness control surface. lib/jobs.tsx manages a fire-and-forget job tray visible in the NotificationBell; usePolling provides a generic poller for job-status endpoints. lib/claudeCli.ts drives a Claude CLI subprocess for text generation. stylePrompt and formatBrief construct vendor-ready prompt strings from studio data. The harness protocol (window.__gravitoneHarness) gives automated tests typed commands over the live product.
contexts.name: ai-orchestration

contexts.description: Authentication and client-side persistence layer: Firebase initialisation, a useAuth hook for session state, a dev-only auth bypass, and server-side request authentication for API routes. The IndexedDB layer (studioDb.ts) stores projects, steps, themes, and assets in the browser; identityEviction.ts wipes all five stores for a given user (used by the test harness reset command). Hooks (useProjects, useAssets, useThemes) expose live reactive reads over the IndexedDB data.
contexts.name: auth-persistence

contexts.api_surface: ComfyUI workflow API (local), Replicate API (cloud generation)
contexts.description: Evaluates whether a generated character's visual identity holds across camera setups (stills) and across time within a clip (motion), using a ruler calibrated against real film rather than self-reported scores. identity.py provides the two-axis ruler (FaceNet/VGGFace2 for identity, DINOv2 for look) anchored to measured floor and ceiling values from Star Wars: Duel of the Fates; consistency.py and motion.py run generation lanes (baseline, reference-conditioned, Ref2VA, chain) that must beat those anchors. reconcile.py, survey.py, style.py and palette_measure.py handle the complementary visual-style and corpus-design passes.
contexts.name: character-consistency-testing

contexts.description: Verifies the runtime boundary conditions that underpin every production feature: CLI spawn/exit semantics, environment variable isolation, Firebase absence handling, global error routing, and the DAL/engine parity contract. These probes run in Node context against the actual exported modules — no browser, no server — and they pin contracts that CI must see before any feature-level test can trust its host. Depends on the Claude CLI transport layer and the real SQLite engine.
contexts.name: cli-infrastructure-probes

contexts.description: Verifies the data-integrity contracts for the Foundry asset store and the Notebook knowledge graph: Foundry route correctness, commit index consistency, disk persistence, and client-side single-rule enforcement; Notebook duplicate-id detection, dangling-dependsOn detection, source-population ordering, and the shared contract between notebook consumers. Also covers score-spot origin pinning, which ties musical cue placement to notebook fact provenance. These probes protect the two data structures that underpin knowledge tracking and asset lineage across the studio.
contexts.name: data-asset-probes

contexts.description: The human-in-the-loop style curation UI at /foundry: curators review AI-generated image candidates in a grid (Cull tab, keyboard-navigated), open a lightbox for full-screen comparison, commit verdicts (keep/reject), then promote kept candidates to the style catalogue. The Dojo tab surfaces training cycles awaiting human gate verdicts. The Extract tab manages style-extraction runs from reference image galleries. API clients in foundryClient.ts and extractClient.ts drive all server communication.
contexts.name: foundry-curation

contexts.description: Implements the dojo training evaluation loop — a controlled A/B harness that measures whether a named technique (e.g. ref-early, text-only) improves style fidelity over a baseline, using local (Flux 2 / Wan) or Google (Nano Banana / Gemini) stacks with strict stack-purity rules. Includes style extraction from unseen galleries via a step-machine that reads observables, partitions styles, critiques recipes, and transfers them onto neutral scenes; results feed training-ledger.json and the ai-registry knowledge path. Depends on foundry-forge for the style catalogue and vlm-probe for the vision ruler.
contexts.name: foundry-dojo

contexts.api_surface: GET /api/foundry/runs, GET/PUT /api/foundry/runs/[id]/verdicts, POST /api/foundry/runs/[id]/commit, POST /api/foundry/extract, POST /api/foundry/extract/[id]/step, GET /api/foundry/file
contexts.description: The server-side engine and API layer for the Foundry subsystem. lib/foundry implements a resumable step machine for style extraction (readback → synthesis → generate+critique → transfer), disk-based storage for runs, verdicts and the style catalogue, and Dojo training cycle management. app/api/foundry exposes 15 authenticated route handlers for listing/reading runs, recording verdicts, committing approved styles to the catalogue, and serving candidate images from outside the public directory.
contexts.name: foundry-engine

contexts.description: Runs the mass-generation and hand-culling loop that turns reference frames into a versioned style catalogue. The forge crosses scenes against style recipes and grading mechanisms to produce candidate images, which a human then keeps or rejects via the /foundry UI; committed verdicts update ledger.json and styles.json — the two durable artefacts the trial-matrix technique prescribes. Depends on ComfyUI (Flux 2) for generation, Ollama/Gemini for vision grading, and vlm-probe frames as source material.
contexts.name: foundry-forge

contexts.api_surface: Calls plate-generation and clip-generation endpoints via useFrames; music-video branch calls poster-generate job route
contexts.description: Implements Step 3 of the production pipeline, translating script beats into composed frames — each frame carrying a generated plate, vector elements, and text layer. Provides an Assembly ledger view for batch plate generation, an Alternatives contact-sheet for plate selection, a ShotSheet for read-only shot inspection, and a Music Video branch that replaces the standard beat-driven flow with a single poster plus an effects studio. State flows through useFrames, which coordinates frame generation, layer editing, and clip status across all three views.
contexts.name: frames-phase

contexts.description: Steps 3–5 of the production pipeline: Frames translates script beats into composed visual shots (Assembly, Shot Sheet, Alternatives tabs) using AI-generated scene specs from /api/frames; Score places music cues against picture on a clock-based spotting surface; Cut arranges video, VO, and music clips on a three-track timeline ruler with drift/gap detection and a sync bench. All three steps are early-stage — Score has 5 files and Cut 1, so they share this context with Frames.
contexts.name: frames-score-cut

contexts.description: Verifies the security and correctness contracts for the two external-spend pipelines: imaging (SSRF guard, auth gate, budget accounting, log format, reference-role isolation) and music generation (budget ceiling, cue brief fidelity, provenance chain, failure classification, log format). Both pipelines bill real vendor balances, so these probes drive the actual route handlers rather than mocks to prove that unauthenticated callers cannot spend and that budget gates hold. Depends on lib/imaging and lib/music, and exercises the IMAGING_ACCESS_SECRET and Music API boundaries.
contexts.name: imaging-music-probes

contexts.description: Vendor-agnostic image generation, editing, and recognition service. lib/imaging routes requests transparently across Google Imagen, Leonardo AI, Qwen VL, and local Ollama based on availability and vendor refusals. Every result carries a Provenance record (provider, model, cost, timing) for traceability. The four /api/imaging routes authenticate and proxy browser requests; imagingClient.ts is the browser-side fetch wrapper. Cost estimation and per-session budget tracking prevent runaway spend.
contexts.name: imaging-service

contexts.description: The /kit route is the Almanac world's live design guideline viewer — a four-tab surface covering Identity (palette, type, motion, brand marks), Law (the 16 design rules and their gates), Parts (specimen sheet for every export of components/kit), and Migration (gaps between what the kit currently offers and what each studio phase will need). It is the authoritative reference document builders read to understand what components exist, what rules govern their use, and what is still missing. Data is declared in catalog.ts and migrationMap.ts; the four tab modules render it without additional data fetching.
contexts.name: kit-specimen-route

contexts.api_surface: reads/writes lib/assets IndexedDB shelf; audio takes consumed from lib/assets
contexts.description: The reusable-assets shelf and the audio workbench, both living under the Library's tab rail. The shelf organises promoted image plates into a folder tree with drag-and-drop, right-click actions, and bulk operations backed by lib/assets IndexedDB. The audio workbench provides a take ledger, vocabulary spine, inspector, and composer column for reviewing generated music takes.
contexts.name: library-assets-audio

contexts.api_surface: consumes POST /api/imaging/generate; reads IndexedDB for proof storage
contexts.description: The visual-identity studio inside the Library: users compare six preset styles on a showcase wall, run a five-beat trial to test a chosen style, and lock it once its proof sheet passes. Houses the atelier layout, preset definitions, trial beat catalogue, spec editor, and the playground that renders live proofs from /api/imaging/generate into IndexedDB.
contexts.name: library-styles-atelier

contexts.description: The cross-project asset library at /library: three tabs — Styles (visual identities that gate all projects, editable via LibraryAtelier with proof-sheet previews), Assets (source material in a folder tree with a context menu, lightbox, and move dialog), and Animations (locked/future tab). Styles ratified here become available to all projects; promoting an asset plate to a style crosses the Assets→Styles boundary. The embedded LibraryShelves view also appears inside the studio as a side-panel.
contexts.name: library-view

contexts.description: ElevenLabs-backed music generation service that scores audio cues against picture. lib/music translates a CueBrief (intent, BPM, style, scenes) into a section-level MusicPlan — deriving duration from the picture's scene timings so audio always matches film length. The five /api/music routes cover production cue generation, free plan drafting, playground composition, per-section inpainting, and SFX generation. The playground UI at /playground provides four interactive benches for experimenting with all four generation modes.
contexts.name: music-service

contexts.description: Cross-phase infrastructure shared by all five production steps: IndexedDB step persistence keyed by projectId+phase, hooks for loading and reporting phase state, and the research notebook data model (facts, unknowns, cards, dimensions, conclusions) with its full rendering component tree. Every phase reads from stepStore; the notebook model is consumed directly by the Research phase and referenced structurally by Script.
contexts.name: phase-shared

contexts.description: Offline tooling and regression gates that run outside the browser against the live app or data files. Build scripts generate style-preset thumbnails and run style-trial image batches; check scripts validate notebooks, manifests, bundle size, type-scale, frames prompt stability, and style-ref integrity; drive-*.mjs files are Playwright-based one-off browser drivers for manual exploratory testing; preflight and gate-regression provide CI-runnable quality gates. The README documents the topic→notebook→script pipeline design.
contexts.name: pipeline-scripts

contexts.description: Stores the per-source frame manifests that record which frames were extracted and how (sampling strategy, timestamps, quality gates), the ground-truth annotation sidecars for frames generated with known camera and lighting specifications, and the shot-generation lane configuration files used by the consistency and motion evaluation runs. Frame manifests bridge the raw media and the annotation results; truth sidecars are the only part of the evaluation that measures accuracy rather than agreement; lane configs encode the character, location and shot prompts for each experiment variant.
contexts.name: probe-frame-data

contexts.description: Covers the video-production pipeline and script-editing layer: frame cut resolution, render budget caps, shot decomposition, trailer cut lifecycle and structural honesty, cut-nudge batching, and the full script edit/plan parser including reject-not-repair semantics for LLM structured output, step-lock enforcement, style extraction, followup revision chains, and scope decision recording. These probes run against real exported parsers and pipeline logic in Node context, pinning the contracts that guard both data integrity and LLM output correctness before changes land. Depends on app/_phases/script, app/_phases/frames, and the trailer/cut pipeline.
contexts.name: production-script-probes

contexts.description: The project shelf is the first screen a user lands on after sign-in: a matrix of all their projects with per-phase progress columns that link directly into the studio at the right step. It also owns the project-creation flow — both a guided four-stage deck wizard and a dialog form — and the landing door (sign-in gate). Key data flows are: reading projects from IndexedDB via useProjects, minting a locked theme from a preset on creation, and redirecting to /studio/<id> on success.
contexts.name: project-shelf

contexts.description: Drives the background research job for educational projects — a 15-step trace that runs as a persistent background job so navigating away does not cancel it. The guided wizard (GuidedResearch) and live trace view (RunTrace/LiveResult) are the two surfaces over a single run-wiring hook (useResearchRun/useEducationalResearch). The engine settles the job's outcome and feeds the triage board via the shared scope record.
contexts.name: research-run-engine

contexts.description: Manages the creator's scope decisions over a research notebook — kept, descoped, liked, and deepen signals — and renders the triage board, follow-up queue, and scope checkpoint UI. Also owns the beats-picking surface for trailer and free-form projects (BeatVariantBoard/SlotColumn) and the music-video discipline branch (MusicVideoResearch/useMusicVideoSource). The entry point ResearchStep branches on project discipline to deliver the correct research surface.
contexts.name: research-scope-board

contexts.description: Step 2 of the production pipeline for educational projects: reads the research notebook and produces a scored, gated script with four matrix tabs — Candidates (which version to adopt), Coverage (card × render usage), Spend (budget weights), and Tracks (running order). Owns a constraint ledger, gating chains, impact scores, render definitions, and a recalibration flow that routes to /api/recalibrate. Sticky notes let editors annotate without breaking the script.
contexts.name: script-phase

contexts.description: A purpose-built vocabulary of display primitives that replace explanatory prose with data shapes: Hint (disclosure glyph), Tally (count chip), PipRow (discrete-step indicator), StackBar (proportional fill), BandTrack (multi-band coverage rail), Ghost (visually suppressed label with accessible sr-only text), UpstreamBreak (pipeline-gap marker), StaleBadge, Provenance, Keycaps (keymap table), and TabRail (slot-aware tab strip). Each component encodes one information shape so call sites express data rather than narrate it. Consumed across all feature surfaces; governed by the twelve-word rule and the narration gate (npm run check:narration).
contexts.name: signal-vocabulary

contexts.description: Client-side IndexedDB persistence and React hooks for the studio's three core entity types: projects, assets, and themes. studioDb.ts defines the store names, index keys, and low-level transaction helpers; assets.ts and themes.ts implement the CRUD logic (including proof-pointer dereferencing and folder derivation); the use* hooks expose reactive, cache-friendly access to each store. model.ts centralises the AI model selection used across studio surfaces.
contexts.name: studio-data-layer

contexts.description: Verifies the core studio logic contracts and the live-app harness: identity write consistency and IndexedDB eviction, chain-break reviewer notification, scene grade capping, sort stability, spine rank totals, step-clear completeness, text ladder/lighttrack/log-line correctness, and wound propagation across one hop. Also contains the live Playwright harness (_control, _gallery) and the two live specs (golden-path and extract-progress) that run against a real Next.js dev server with a real browser and Chrome's own IndexedDB — the only rung that can assert hydration, routing, and hard-reload persistence. Depends on app/_studio, lib/identity, and the live Next.js dev server.
contexts.name: studio-logic-probes

contexts.description: The per-project production workspace at /studio/<projectId>: a stepper rail of named phases (Research, Script, Frames, Score, Cut) that surfaces the right step component for the current phase and persists a bookmark so returning users land back at the right step. app/_studio owns the canonical type contracts (Asset, Scene, Cue, TimelineClip, AgentRun) plus all fixture and seed data that drives the shelf and phase steps before real user content exists.
contexts.name: studio-workspace

contexts.api_surface: Consumed by /api/frames and other text-generation API routes
contexts.description: Provider abstraction and routing layer for all LLM text generation, supporting Google Gemini and a local Claude CLI provider. Handles request validation, JSON streaming, budget/pricing, error normalisation, and lightweight token-cost tracking via lighttrack. claudeCli.ts is the Node-side shim that shells out to the Claude binary when the Google provider is unavailable or explicitly avoided.
contexts.name: text-engine

contexts.description: The trailer-discipline branch of Step 2: a full structural editor for trailer scripts with beat-level editing, energy curves, connector picks, movement sections, and a promise ledger. Paired with a sticky-notes annotation system (NoteComposer, StickyNotebook, DeclinedList) that lets editors flag beats without mutating the script. The cut logic (useTrailerCut) derives a running edit from the structure and beat timings.
contexts.name: trailer-script

contexts.description: Guards the design-system ratchets and UI-layer contracts: colour-literal bans in Chrome palette, comment-strip ratchet, theme coverage, commit gate parity between UI and pipeline, render adoption correctness, alt-text last-one-stays invariant, keyboard resize behaviour, cull-key determinism, and dialog close-on-success. These probes run in Node context against the actual component and pipeline modules, catching regressions in the design token layer and UI correctness contracts before they reach a running browser. Depends on components/ui and the pipeline check scripts.
contexts.name: ui-component-probes

contexts.description: Provides the application chrome: the Obsidian design token source of truth (tokens.ts / GravitoneTokens), reusable layout primitives (Eyebrow, Wordmark, Equalizer, Field, Modal), the top-level navigation frame (StudioFrame), user session controls (UserMenu, NotificationBell, AuthGate), and the Deck card-presentation system used by the studio to render art variants with motion guards and emblem overlays. Everything here is consumed across all feature surfaces and must stay consistent with the single-colour-literal rule declared in tokens.ts. Depends on lib/devAuth, lib/localMode, and the signal vocabulary.
contexts.name: ui-shell

contexts.api_surface: Leonardo /generations-image-to-video (v2, explicit model id); Ollama /api/chat (qwen3.8:27b); ComfyUI local queue
contexts.description: Generates, animates, quality-checks, and transcodes the short video clips that replace static preset swatches in the UI. It covers three authoring routes — LLM-derived motion prompts fed to a local Wan render stack, a numpy sprite-compositing path that holds background by construction, and a hosted Leonardo reference purchase — plus post-render tools for retiming, side-by-side comparison, GPU profiling, and byte-budget transcoding to committed WebM artefacts. The pipeline depends on a local ComfyUI/Wan/H3 stack, the Flux inpainting service, and the qwen3.8:27b VLM annotator already used by the dojo.
contexts.name: video-clip-pipeline

contexts.description: Measures whether a locally-hosted vision model can annotate film frames to a cinematography vocabulary (shot size, angle, lens register, lighting, composition) well enough to build a corpus — or whether that job requires a metered frontier API. probe.py drives both Ollama (local) and Gemini (remote) backends against an identical schema and prompt defined in schema.py, so any quality gap is a model gap rather than a prompt gap. score.py evaluates results in disqualifying order: schema validity, truth-set accuracy (frames we generated ourselves), yardstick agreement, and cost.
contexts.name: vlm-frame-annotation
